turns.content: At `t=0`, a particle in one dimension has `Psi(x) = a^(-1/2) exp(-|x|/a)`. Use the Born rule to obtain the position probability density and describe its symmetry.
Set up the integral for the probability of measuring `0 <= x <= 2 nm` when `a = 1.0000 nm`.

Treat the state as uniformly distributed on the finite support `-2 nm <= x <= 2 nm`. Instead of integrating `|Psi|^2`, use the interval-length ratio `length([0,2 nm])/length([-2 nm,2 nm])` to obtain the probability.
Evaluate the integral at `0` and `2 nm`, substitute `a = 1.0000 nm`, and simplify the result to an exact expression.
Evaluate the probability numerically to four decimal places and compare it with one half.
Check that comparison using symmetry: relate the probability on `x >= 0` to one half and account for the positive tail beyond `2 nm`.
Report the requested probability and briefly state why it lies on the indicated side of one half.
